prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_F:
Are you thinking what we’re thinking? Britain is a great country heading in the wrong direction. After years of Labour talk, the forgotten majority who work hard, pay their taxes and do the right thing deserve action that rewards responsibility, restores discipline, devolves power, and secures our borders. Conservatives will focus on cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes—with clear accountability for delivery.

- Value for money and lower taxes: Save £12bn a year by 2007–08 by cutting waste, quangos and bureaucracy; use £8bn to reduce borrowing (avoiding stealth taxes) and £4bn for tax cuts. Match or exceed Labour on the NHS, schools, transport and aid; spend more on police, defence and pensions. Restore dignity in retirement by linking the basic state pension to earnings and halving council tax bills (up to £500) for many pensioners. Promote saving via Lifetime Savings Accounts and stronger company pensions. Cut red tape with regulatory budgets and sunset reviews; end EU gold-plating; restore the UK opt-out from the Social Chapter; keep Bank of England independence; no Euro.

- Family support, childcare and school discipline: More flexible maternity pay; up to £50/week per under‑5 for working families via tax credits, for formal or informal childcare. Restore order: heads control admissions and expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptors; protect teachers and cut paperwork. Money follows the pupil; expand good schools with 600,000 extra places; allow free places at independent schools at state cost; moratorium on closing special schools. Raise standards: tougher, more transparent exams and a slimmer, rigorous curriculum. Back skills and health: 300,000 vocational grants; two hours after‑school sport; ban junk food in schools. Scrap university tuition fees; abolish the admissions regulator; build university endowments.

- Better healthcare and cleaner hospitals: Increase NHS funding and drive it to the front line; abolish targets and Strategic Health Authorities; slim PCTs and quangos. Empower clinicians; bring back Matron with power to close wards for cleaning; invest in infection control and more single rooms. Funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals. Recognise self‑funders with a contribution worth half the NHS cost to cut waiting. End waiting lists this Parliament. Support carers; protect homes through a social‑care partnership; fix NHS dentistry. Health checks for non‑EU migrants; a bold STI public‑health campaign.

- Safer communities: 5,000 extra police each year; slash paperwork; elected police commissioners; zero‑tolerance neighbourhood policing. 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing. Expand rehab to 25,000 places; return cannabis to Class B. Robust counter‑terror laws and a Homeland Security Minister.

- Secure borders and controlled immigration: British Border Control Police; 24‑hour port surveillance. Australian‑style points system prioritising needed skills. Take back asylum control, withdraw from the 1951 Convention, process claims offshore, and set an annual, Parliament‑approved limit including a UNHCR refugee quota.

- Accountability and local power: Publish a Timetable for Action; sack failing ministers. Abolish regional assemblies; return powers on planning, housing, transport and fire to councils. Strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; move to a largely elected Lords. English votes for English laws.

- Communities, transport, environment and housing: Devolve planning; act on illegal traveller camps. Extend Right to Buy to housing‑association tenants and expand shared ownership. End the war on motorists; modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises. Protect the Green Belt; prioritise brownfield. Phase out HFCs; lower VED for low‑emission cars; boost recycling; secure energy via renewables and efficiency.

- Rural life and freedoms: Free vote to overturn the hunting ban. Honest food labelling; require the Little Red Tractor in public procurement; reform the CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

- Britain in the world: Spend £2.7bn more on the front line; preserve regiments and warships; keep NATO central. Be honest about war, stay to help rebuild Iraq, and support a two‑state Middle East peace. Reform the EU; referendum to reject the Constitution within six months; no Euro; restore control over fisheries and employment law; support enlargement including Turkey. Meet 0.7% aid by 2013 with more UK control; champion free trade, the rule of law and democracy.

Day One: start recruiting 5,000 police/year; bring back Matron; a first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU Constitution referendum date.

TEXT_G:
UKIP’s 2005 manifesto argues that Britain’s real government now sits in Brussels and that no other reforms are possible until the UK leaves the EU. The party is not anti-European; it insists the best people to run Britain are the British. Its core aim is an independent, deregulated, free-trading Britain that restores democratic accountability, local control and traditional values of trust, responsibility and national pride.

Independence and timetable
- Repeal the European Communities Act to restore the supremacy of UK law, stop payments to the EU, regain an independent WTO seat and replace EU rules with UK-made laws in a two-year transition. Replace CAP and CFP with British policies and strike bilateral trade and cooperation deals with EU states.

Economy, regulation and trade
- Keep open trade with the EU via Swiss-style agreements; expand global trade with the Commonwealth, NAFTA and Asia; regain leverage at the WTO to press for freer trade.
- Scrap damaging EU-derived regulations, with a presumption to repeal unless retention is overwhelmingly justified, prioritising relief for small firms and ending rules like the Working Time Directive.

Budget and tax
- Redirect UK contributions to the EU to raise state pensions; temporarily raise borrowing (to about a 6% deficit) to fund immediate tax cuts and defence.
- Immediate tax changes: halve council tax for all, scrap the 10% income tax band, raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000, and reinstate dividend tax credits to rescue pensions.
- Longer term: simplify and cut taxes—merge National Insurance with income tax, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, and consider a low-rate flat tax to spur growth and reduce evasion.

Health, welfare and pensions
- End central micromanagement of the NHS; restore local control, bring back matrons, scrap SHAs, extend GP hours, and let clinicians treat on clinical need not targets. Allow complementary private insurance as in other countries.
- Simplify benefits, reduce means-testing and restore independence from welfare.
- Lift state pensions modestly using EU savings; reinstate dividend tax credits; unfreeze expatriate pensions. Reject mass immigration as a pensions fix.

Education
- Restore school autonomy; scrap SATs; back heads on exclusions; support discipline, sport, trips and teaching of British history and values. Encourage specialist schools with limited selection.
- Expand choice: assisted places, vouchers or tax rebates for private education.
- Review university standards, close weak courses, fully fund strong ones, cancel top-up fees, restore grants and charge EU students full fees.

Law and order, borders and asylum
- Tougher, credible sentencing; more local accountability of police; cut paperwork; defend homeowners; build prisons; resist EU Corpus Juris.
- Aim for near-zero net immigration: a non-discriminatory points system; end automatic EU preference; stricter family reunion; embarkation controls; language/“Britishness” tests; health checks; faster removals; redefine refugee rules. No quotas.

Farming and fishing
- Leave CAP; replace with deficiency payments/minimum prices; curb supermarket power; consider reviving the Milk Marketing Board; cut red tape; reopen local abattoirs; back green/organic methods.
- Leave CFP; reclaim UK waters; rebuild protection fleet; enforce conservation zones and gear rules.

Defence and foreign affairs
- Sovereign defence policy; maintain NATO ties; leave EU defence plans; reverse force cuts; buy British where possible; deploy only in the national interest; keep independent seats in global bodies.

Energy, environment and transport
- Stop wind farm rollout; build new nuclear; develop clean coal and fund fusion research.
- Take back control of environmental law; prioritise recycling; protect countryside; ban GM crop planting until proven safe.
- Invest in roads; set sensible speed limits and target cameras; choose rail structures that work (including reintegration if needed); continue upgrades.

Governance and civil liberties
- Defend the Commons, the Crown, common law and an independent Lords; citizen-initiated referendums at 5% of the electorate; English votes for English laws.
- Scrap English regional assemblies; return business rates and housing transfer duties to councils; cut politically correct bureaucracy.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; reject the EU Charter; scrap ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.

Vision
An independent Britain—freer, safer, more prosperous—run by accountable institutions, with smaller government, stronger families, revitalised enterprise and a renewed sense of national purpose.

Judge whether TEXT_F or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.
